"I want you to create a game about being a gritty, hard-boiled 1940s noir detective solving randomized murder mysteries late at night. 

Here is how the game works and what you need to build:
- Visuals @COMMENT_BODY@ Atmosphere: Dark, moody noir aesthetic with rain, shadows, and dramatic lighting. Keep all text descriptions short, punchy, and under two sentences—no long paragraphs.
- Randomized Cases: Every time a new game starts, randomly generate a new Victim, a Murder Weapon, 3 Suspects (with motives and alibis), 4 Clues (including 1 definitive \"Smoking Gun\" clue that proves who did it), and 1 True Killer.
- Stage 1 - The Call: Start the game in a dark detective office with a rotary phone ringing at 2:00 AM. Give the player the crime scene address and a short tip from Sergeant Miller, with a button to [Head to the Crime Scene].
- Stage 2 - Top-Down Crime Scene: Show a top-down view of the crime scene room with 4 clickable/tappable objects (such as a desk, a shattered window, a coat, or a safe).
- Stage 3 - The Zoom-In: When the player taps an object, zoom in to a detailed close-up view of that object and reveal one clue with a single gritty sentence describing what was found. Include a button to [Zoom Out].
- Stage 4 - The Evidence Board: Always show a button to [Open Evidence Board]. On the Evidence Board screen, display all clues discovered so far, profile cards for the 3 suspects, and buttons to [Accuse a Suspect] or [Return to Crime Scene].
- Win/Loss Conditions: If the player accuses the wrong suspect, or tries to accuse the right suspect without having found the \"Smoking Gun\" clue first, trigger a Game Over screen where the killer escapes and the case goes cold. If the player finds the \"Smoking Gun\" and accuses the true killer, trigger a Victory screen where the killer is arrested.

Make sure the game is specifically designed for vertical mobile not pc, so no scrolling

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

JS part: ``` const app = $('#app'); const state = {...}; function currentHasGun(){ return state.found.has(gunObject) } ``` Find gun object: `Object.values(caseData.clues).find(c=>c.type==='gun').object`. `showScreen(name)`: - map name to id. set classes. - app.dataset.scene = name; - state.screen=name; - live region message. - if name !== 'office' Sfx.stopRing(); else Sfx.startRing (if enabled). - if name==='board' renderBoard(); - if name==='accuse' renderAccuse(); - if name==='scene' renderScene(); - if name==='zoom'... - reset scroll none. - manage sound ring. - For end, add classes. Need showScreen called after render for board/accuse. Important transitions: `.screen` transition with visibility .5s. On show, content. Fine. `renderCase` updates all IDs: ``` $('#officeCaseNo').textContent = `#${id}`; $('#millerLine').textContent = `“${tip}”`; ... ``` Scene victim: `${victim.name}` plus maybe role in sub. I have HUD sub "VICTIM — ". Set b to "Arthur Vale, nightclub owner". At 8px, could be long but max-width 230 ellipsis. Fine. Scene place: location.name. boardVictim name; boardVictimRole role. accuseCaseNo, boardCaseNo, sceneCaseNo, endCaseNo. - sceneArt.dataset.place. `renderSceneState`: ``` $$('.hotspot').forEach(btn=>{ const key = btn.dataset.object; const found = state.found.has(key); btn.classList.toggle('found',found); btn.querySelector('.tag').textContent = found ? `${OBJECTS[key].short} ✓` : OBJECTS[key].short; btn.setAttribute('aria-label', `${found?'Review':'Inspect'} ${OBJECTS[key].name}`); }); $('#clueProgress').textContent = `${state.found.size} OF 4 CLUES LOGGED`; ``` Maybe when 0 use "0 OF 4 CLUES LOGGED". Yes. Show a hint "4 OF 4 · OPEN THE BOARD" when all found? Clue progress could be. Keep. `openObject`: ``` const first = !state.found.has(key); state.currentObject=key; state.found.add(key); renderZoom(); showScreen('zoom'); if(first){ flash(); Sfx.clue(letter?); } ``` Flash via function: ``` function cameraFlash(){const f=$('#flash'); f.classList.remove('on'); void f.offsetWidth; f.classList.add('on');} ``` Sfx clue if enabled. `renderZoom`: - guard currentObject. - `clue` from caseData. - set text. - `clueSheet.classList.toggle('is-gun', type==='gun')` - gunTag hidden by CSS. - Set zoomCanvas innerHTML. Add closeup SVG. The art uses IDs; only one at a time. - set object labels. - `zoomFound` `${found.size} / 4`. - Set `zoomExhibit`: `EXHIBIT ${obj.exhibit} · ${obj.short}`. - plate. - Set `zoomArt.dataset.object`. - `#zoomArt` has `aria-label`? Set. - also log small status. - View: class .is-gun. `renderBoard`: Build HTML. Use tilt array based on object index: [-.35,.25,-.15,.4]. `--tilt`. Use `--i`. Locked cards show `CLUE 01 · DESK` and "NOT YET LOGGED — INSPECT THE {short}" maybe. Keep text "NOT YET LOGGED". Maybe "CLUE NOT YET LOGGED". Remember requirement 4 clues including gun; board shows all slots locked. - Escaping text via esc. - suspect portraits. - Suspect row maybe add no data; board list display. Fine. - If clues found, gun card red tag. `renderAccuse`: - state.selected reset when entering? It persists maybe. Set null each time to force deliberate selection. Yes renderAccuse sets state.selected=null unless passed preserve? On entering from board, reset. On clicking back from confirm, preserve. We call renderAccuse on entering; don't call when selecting. So set state.selected = null at render. Good. - HTML rows. - update button & warning after. - `setSelected(index)` updates classes, button disabled, text; ensure no re-render. - Make accusation opens confirm; if selected. - Do accuse evaluate: ``` const correct = state.selected === caseData.killerIndex; const hasGun = ...; const win = correct && hasGun; showEnd(win, {correct, hasGun}); ``` - `state.failure = !correct ? 'wrong' : !hasGun ? 'no-gun' : null`. `showEnd`: Detailed set. Classes on `#screen-end`. ``` end.classList.toggle('is-win', win); ... endStamp.textContent = win?'CASE CLOSED':'CASE COLD'; endHeadline = win?'The bracelets clicked.':'The killer walked.'; endCopy = ... endKillerLabel ... endKiller ... endVictim = `${victim.name} — ${victim.role}` maybe em dash; endWeapon = `a ${weapon}`; endNail.innerHTML = `THE NAIL ${esc(gun.text)}`; // text under 2 sentences ... showScreen('end') cameraFlash on win ``` For loss no gun: copy "You had the right name and empty hands. {killer} walked before the ink was dry." 2 sentences. For wrong: "The wrong name bought {killer} a clean getaway. By dawn, the trail was rain." Actually if wrong, the true killer is revealed but "the wrong name bought ..." nice. Win copy: "{killer} didn't say a word on the ride downtown. The city can sleep—for one night." 2 sentences. Hmm gritty. Good. Headline maybe "The bracelets clicked." nice. End weather text. Loss label "TRUE KILLER"; win "ARRESTED". End nail label; if lose and hadn't found gun, the smoking gun clue reveal. If wrong but had gun, also reveal. Good. Board open buttons [data-open-board] all. Sound button. Back etc. Escape. Prevent confirm overlay click outside closing? clicking background could close. ## Objective
- Build a complete, playable vertical-mobile noir detective game about solving randomized 1940s murder mysteries.

## Requirements
- Dark, moody noir atmosphere with rain, shadows, and dramatic lighting; descriptions under two sentences.
- Each new case randomizes a victim, weapon, three suspects with motives/alibis, four clues including a definitive smoking gun, and the true killer.
- Gameplay stages: 2:00 AM phone call, top-down scene with four inspectable objects, close-up clue reveal, evidence board, accusation, and win/loss screens.
- Accusing incorrectly or accusing before finding the smoking gun loses; correctly accusing after finding it wins.
- Designed for vertical mobile with no scrolling.

## Decisions
- Built from scratch as a static HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with locally bundled fonts and custom SVG artwork.
- Added optional user-enabled synthesized rain/phone audio; no external runtime dependencies.

## Work State

### Completed
- Implemented randomized cases, four interactive objects/clues, evidence board, suspect accusation flow, and victory/game-over logic.
- Built noir office, crime-scene, close-up, board, accusation, and end-screen views with mobile-focused styling.
- Tested several screens using mobile-sized Playwright screenshots; fixed a win-screen null-reference issue and refined layouts.
- Added booking/last-known portrait card to the end screen in the latest changes.

### Active
- Validate the latest end-screen portrait changes and retest full game flow, including correct accusation with smoking gun and incorrect accusation / missing smoking gun.
- Check responsive no-scroll layout and JavaScript syntax after the latest edits.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `node --check game.js` and inspect the latest changes for runtime errors.
2. Use a mobile viewport to verify end screens and both win/loss paths, plus board/scene layout.
3. Fix any issues found; summarize assumptions and checks when finishing.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens, scene/object markup, evidence board, accusation and end-screen structure.
- `game.js`: Case generation, clues, state, rendering, game flow, optional sound, and end-screen behavior.
- `styles.css`: Noir visuals, animations, and vertical mobile layouts.
- `fonts/`: Locally bundled fonts used by the game.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no commit or push was reported.

## Objective
- Build and polish a playable vertical-mobile noir detective game about solving randomized 1940s murder mysteries.
- Improve the office scene, lamp, and phone, and make the phone ring, answer on tap, and lead into sergeant dialogue.

## Requirements
- Dark, moody noir atmosphere with rain, shadows, and dramatic lighting; descriptions under two sentences.
- Each case randomizes a victim, weapon, three suspects with motives/alibis, four clues including a smoking gun, and the true killer.
- Stages: 2:00 AM call, top-down crime scene with four inspectable objects, clue reveal, evidence board, accusation, and win/loss screens.
- Incorrect accusation or accusing without the smoking gun loses; correct accusation after finding it wins.
- Vertical mobile layout with no scrolling.
- Office should look better; lamp and phone should be visually improved.
- Phone must ring, be tappable to pick up, then display the sergeant's dialogue lines.
- Ringing sound should be better and remain optional/user-enabled.

## Decisions
- Static HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with locally bundled fonts and custom SVG artwork.
- Audio remains optional and synthesized; no external runtime dependencies.
- Office call is now interactive and gated: the scene button stays disabled until the phone is answered and Miller's dialogue/address is completed.
- Phone is a real accessible button; office content uses `pointer-events:none` with interactive children re-enabled so taps reach the phone.

## Work State
### Completed
- Randomized cases, clue logic, evidence board, accusation flow, and victory/game-over logic.
- Noir office, crime scene, close-up, board, accusation, and end-screen views.
- End-screen booking-portrait card styling and short-screen variants.
- Fixed `.device`/`.screen` internal focus scrolling by using `overflow:clip`, preventing clipped screens.
- Upgraded office visuals: wall treatment, window mullions/droplets/sill, richer desk, dust motes, and lamp glow.
- Replaced the lamp with a detailed SVG banker's lamp with brass frame, base, pull chain, and warm bulb glow.
- Replaced the phone with a detailed SVG rotary phone: dial, numbers, handset, cord, highlights, and shadow.
- Added ringing animation, ring arcs, `TAP TO ANSWER` hint, and handset pickup animation.
- Added `state.call` plus `buildCallLines`, `resetCall`, `renderCallLine`, `answerPhone`, `finishCall`, and `advanceCall`.
- Added three sequential Miller dialogue lines, line counter, `NEXT`/`TAKE THE ADDRESS` action, address reveal, and updated clock/kicker.
- Improved synthesized ring with metallic bell partials, tremolo, and clapper click; added pickup thunk/static.
- Verified `node --check game.js` and full Playwright flows at `390×844`, `360×640`, and `320×568`, including win path, call reset, no-scroll layout, and audio enable/disable.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. (none)

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Office markup, phone/lamp SVGs, call dialogue card, other game screens.
- `game.js`: Case generation, call state/flow, audio synthesis, clue/board/accusation logic.
- `styles.css`: Office/noir artwork, phone/lamp styling, responsive layout, end-screen cards.
- `fonts/`: Locally bundled fonts used throughout the game.

## Important Context
- All current changes are uncommitted; no commit or push was made.
- Key office IDs: `#phoneZone`, `#phoneHint`, `#callCard`, `#callStatus`, `#callIdle`, `#callDialogue`, `#callLine`, `#callStep`, `#btnCallNext`, `#callAddress`, `#officeKicker`, `#officeSub`, `#btnSceneLabel`.

- `Sfx.startRing()` is gated by `state.call.answered`; toggling sound on after answering must not restart ringing.
- On short screens, answered state shifts `.office-lamp` and `.phone-zone` upward to keep them above the taller dialogue card.

function renderScene(loc) {
  const scene = SCENES[loc.scene];
  const pal = SCENE_PALETTES[scene.palette || loc.scene] || {};
  const vars = Object.entries(pal).map(([k,v]) => `--${k}:${v}`).join(';');
  const floor = `url(#rs-p-${scene.floor || 'wood'})`;
  let out = `<svg class="room-svg" viewBox="0 0 400 500" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice" aria-hidden="true" style="${vars}">${SCENE_DEFS}`;
  out += `<rect width="400" height="500" fill="${floor}"/>`;
  // floor vignette maybe
  out += (scene.lights||[]).map(...).join('');
  out += drawWalls(scene);
  out += (scene.wallProps||[]).map(drawProp).join('');
  out += (scene.props||[]).map(drawProp).join('');
  out += drawBody(scene.body || [200,275,0]);
  out += Object.values(scene.stations).map(st => STATIONS[st.t].draw(st)).join('');
  out += (scene.foreground||[]).map(drawProp).join('');
  if (scene.sign) out += SIGNS[scene.sign.style]({...scene.sign, top:loc.plate?.[0], main:loc.plate?.[1]});
  out += `<rect width="400" height="500" fill="url(#rs-vignette)" pointer-events="none"/>`;
  out += `</svg>`;
  return out;
}

const SCENE_FLOORS = {

  hex: 'rs-p-hex', stone: 'rs-p-stone', brick: 'rs-p-brick', concrete: 'rs-p-concrete',

const SCENE_WALLS = {
  paper: 'rs-w-paper', panel: 'rs-w-panel', tile: 'rs-w-tile', brick: 'rs-w-brick',
  stone: 'rs-w-stone', metal: 'rs-w-metal', curtain: 'rs-w-curtain', books: 'rs-w-books',
  pipes: 'rs-w-pipes', plaster: 'rs-w-plaster'
};

function sceneWalls(scene) {
  const wallFill = `var(--wall)`;
  const pat = SCENE_WALLS[scene.wall] || 'rs-w-panel';
  const door = scene.door || { x: 156, w: 88, style: 'wood' };
  const dx = door.x, dw = door.w;
  const bands = `
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="400" height="23" fill="${wallFill}"/>
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="21" height="500" fill="${wallFill}"/>
    <rect x="379" y="0" width="21" height="500" fill="${wallFill}"/>
    <rect x="0" y="477" width="${dx}" height="23" fill="${wallFill}"/>
    <rect x="${dx + dw}" y="477" width="${400 - dx - dw}" height="23" fill="${wallFill}"/>
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="400" height="23" fill="url(#${pat})"/>
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="21" height="500" fill="url(#${pat})"/>
    <rect x="379" y="0" width="21" height="500" fill="url(#${pat})"/>
    <rect x="0" y="477" width="${dx}" height="23" fill="url(#${pat})"/>
    <rect x="${dx + dw}" y="477" width="${400 - dx - dw}" height="23" fill="url(#${pat})"/>
    <g fill="var(--wallHi)" opacity=".5">
      <rect x="21" y="20" width="358" height="3"/>
      <rect x="18" y="23" width="3" height="454"/>
      <rect x="379" y="23" width="3" height="454"/>
      <rect x="21" y="474" width="${dx - 21}" height="3"/>
      <rect x="${dx + dw}" y="474" width="${379 - dx - dw}" height="3"/>
    </g>
    <g fill="#000" opacity=".35">
      <rect x="0" y="23" width="400" height="4"/>
      <rect x="21" y="0" width="4" height="500"/>
      <rect x="375" y="0" width="4" height="500"/>
    </g>`;
  const doorArt = () => {
    if (door.style === 'none') {
      return `<rect x="${dx}" y="477" width="${dw}" height="23" fill="var(--wall)"/><rect x="${dx}" y="477" width="${dw}" height="23" fill="url(#${pat})"/>`;
    }
    const metal = door.style === 'metal';
    const fill = metal ? 'var(--metal)' : 'var(--wood)';
    const leaf = `<polygon points="${dx + 5},477 ${dx + 19},438 ${dx + dw - 18},440 ${dx + dw - 5},477" fill="${fill}" stroke="#120c09" stroke-width="1.3"/>
      <polygon points="${dx + 13},470 ${dx + 22},445 ${dx + dw - 21},447 ${dx + dw - 13},470" fill="#000" opacity=".22"/>
      <path d="M${dx + 18} 474 L${dx + 27} 450" stroke="var(--wallHi)" stroke-width="1" opacity=".35"/>
      <circle cx="${dx + dw - 22}" cy="460" r="2.4" fill="var(--metalHi)" opacity=".8"/>`;
    return `<rect x="${dx}" y="477" width="${dw}" height="23" fill="#070809"/>
      <ellipse cx="${dx + dw / 2}" cy="481" rx="${dw * .45}" ry="9" fill="#d9b477" opacity=".07"/>
      ${leaf}`;
  };
  return bands + doorArt();
}

/* ---------- renderer ---------- */
function renderScene(loc) {
  const scene = (typeof SCENES !== 'undefined' && SCENES[loc.scene]) || {};

    `<ellipse cx="${x}" cy="${y}" rx="${rx}" ry="${ry}" fill="${color}" filter="url(#rs-blur)"/>`).join('');
  const wallProps = (scene.wallProps || []).map(drawSceneProp).join('');
  const props = (scene.props || []).map(drawSceneProp).join('');
  const stationLayer = Object.entries(scene.stations || {})
    .map(([key, st]) => {
      const def = STATIONS[st.t];
      return def ? def.draw(st, key) : '';
    }).join('');
  const sign = scene.sign
    ? (SCENE_SIGNS[scene.sign.style] || SCENE_SIGNS.enamel)({
        ...scene.sign,
        top: loc.plate?.[0] || loc.room || '',
        main: loc.plate?.[1] || ''
      })
    : '';
  const foreground = (scene.foreground || []).map(drawSceneProp).join('');

  return `<svg class="room-svg" viewBox="0 0 400 500" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice" aria-hidden="true" style="${sceneVars(pal)}">

    ${stationLayer}

    <rect width="400" height="500" fill="url(#rs-vignette)" pointer-events="none"/>
  </svg>`;
}

function drawSceneProp(p) {
  if (!p || !p.p) return '';
  const fn = PROPS[p.p];

}

function getStationMeta(loc, key) {
  const scene = (typeof SCENES !== 'undefined' && SCENES[loc.scene]) || {};
  const st = scene.stations?.[key];

}

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and polish a playable vertical-mobile noir detective game about solving randomized 1940s murder mysteries.
- Now make every crime scene a visibly different place, with many varied locations, and place the room/pier number or name that Sergeant Miller says somewhere inside the scene.

## Requirements
- Dark, moody noir atmosphere with rain, shadows, and dramatic lighting; descriptions under two sentences.
- Each case randomizes victim, weapon, three suspects with motives/alibis, four clues including a smoking gun, and the true killer.
- Stages: 2:00 AM call, top-down crime scene with four inspectable objects, clue reveal, evidence board, accusation, win/loss.
- Incorrect accusation or accusing without the smoking gun loses; correct accusation after finding it wins.
- Vertical mobile layout with no scrolling.
- Office, lamp, phone, ringing, pickup, and sergeant dialogue must remain as previously improved.
- Crime scenes must not reuse the same room: "make a bunch of different places... I mean alot."
- The number/address Miller mentions (e.g. "Pier 3", "hotel room 808") must appear in the scene so each place feels distinct.

## Decisions
- Static HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with locally bundled fonts and custom SVG artwork.
- Audio remains optional and synthesized; no external runtime dependencies.
- Scene art is now modular, generated from a shared renderer plus palettes, ambient props, four focal stations, body outline, and in-world signage.
- Each location maps to one unique scene composition (target: 24 locations/scenes), with station skins varying by place (desk/bar/chart table, window/porthole/stage door, coat/oilskins/apron, safe/register/locker).
- Scene art split into multiple JS modules instead of one oversized file.

## Work State
### Completed
- Randomized cases, clue logic, evidence board, accusation flow, victory/game-over logic.
- Noir office, crime scene, close-up, board, accusation, and end-screen views.
- End-screen booking-portrait card styling and short-screen variants.
- Fixed `.device`/`.screen` internal focus scrolling with `overflow:clip`.
- Office visual upgrade, banker's lamp SVG, rotary phone SVG, ringing animation, ring arcs, `TAP TO ANSWER`, handset pickup animation.
- Interactive call flow: `state.call`, `buildCallLines`, `resetCall`, `renderCallLine`, `answerPhone`, `finishCall`, `advanceCall`; three Miller lines, address reveal, scene button gated until call done.
- Improved synthesized ring with metallic partials, tremolo, and clapper click; pickup thunk/static; audio toggle does not restart ring after answering.
- Verified earlier at `390×844`, `360×640`, `320×568`: win path, call reset, no-scroll layout, audio enable/disable.
- Created `scene-core.js`: 24 palettes (`SCENE_PALETTES`), shared SVG defs/patterns, `sceneWalls`, `sceneBody`, 10 sign styles (`enamel`, `brass`, `painted`, `stencil`, `neon`, `hanging`, `marquee`, `tent`, `stone`, `air`), `renderScene(loc)`, `getStationMeta`, `getStationPoint`, `drawSceneProp`.
- Created `scene-props.js`: `PROPS` registry with ~35 ambient props (rug, bed, cot, stand, dresser, chair, couch, crates, barrel, rope, counter, stools, jukebox, booth, screen, rail, rack, mic, neon, shelves, boat, water, ringBuoy, chandelier, pews, cross, car, toolWall, drums, plants, plantBench, gurney, jars, piano, trash, fireEscape, puddle, column, statue, stanchions, cart).
- Created `scene-stations.js`: `windowBase` plus 18 desk variants (`writingDesk`, `barTop`, `chartTable`, `dinerTable`, `vanityTable`, `workbench`, `trainTable`, `console`, `glassCounter`, `cardTable`, `altarTable`, `pottingBench`, `metalTable`, `readingTable`, `crateTable`, `foldingTable`, `washstand`, `projectorBench`) and 18 window/door variants (`rainWindow`, `neonWindow`, `cityWindow`, `storefront`, `porthole`, `barredWindow`, `highWindow`, `frostedWindow`, `stainedGlass`, `archedWindow`, `trainWindow`, `studioGlass`, `boothWindow`, `shopWindow`, `glassPanel`, `stageDoor`, `backDoor`, `rollDoor`).
- Fixed palette CSS variables to kebab-case via `sceneVars` camelCase conversion and replaced camelCase `var()` references.

### Active
- Building remaining coat and safe station variants in `scene-stations2.js`.
- Building `scenes.js` with 24 scene specs (floor, wall, lights, props, body position, four station placements, sign style/position).
- Integrating new scene renderer into `index.html`, `game.js`, and `styles.css`.
- Verifying every scene visually and ensuring hotspots, tags, clues, and no-scroll layout still work.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Create `scene-stations2.js` with coat variants (`coatChair`, `coatHook`, `coatRack`, `costumeRack`, `oilskins`, `apron`, `stole`, `uniform`, `vestment`, `smock`, `labCoat`, `coveralls`, `guard`) and safe variants (`wallSafe`, `floorSafe`, `strongbox`, `register`, `locker`, `cashBox`, `cage`, `trunk`, `poorBox`, `displayCase`, `cabinet`, `cardCatalog`, `filmCabinet`, `till`).
2. Fix `getStationMeta` fallback to use a proper default map (`desk → writingDesk`, `window → rainWindow`, `coat → coatChair`, `safe → wallSafe`).
3. Create `scenes.js` with specs for the 24 planned locations.
4. Update `index.html`: replace static hotel scene SVG with `<div id="sceneCanvas">`, load scene modules before `game.js`.
5. Update `game.js`: expand `LOCATIONS`, render scene on case start, set hotspot positions/labels from station metadata, generate clue text from station `place` phrases, use station labels on board/zoom, avoid repeating previous location.
6. Update `styles.css` for `.scene-canvas` and per-scene hotspot positioning; remove/override fixed `.hotspot[data-object]` positions.
7. Run Playwright across all 24 scenes at multiple viewports, capture screenshots, fix overlaps/visual issues, then rerun full win flow.

## Relevant Files
- `scene-core.js`: palettes, room shell, body outline, signage styles, `renderScene`, station metadata helpers.
- `scene-props.js`: all ambient prop SVG drawing functions.
- `scene-stations.js`: desk and window/door station variants (coat/safe still to be added).
- `scenes.js` (to create): 24 scene layout specs.
- `scene-stations2.js` (to create): coat and safe station variants.
- `game.js`: case generation, clue text, locations, scene/hotspot integration, zoom/board labels.
- `index.html`: replace hardcoded hotel scene art; add scene module script tags.
- `styles.css`: `.scene-canvas`, hotspot positioning, scene tag sizing, responsive rules.
- `fonts/`: locally bundled fonts used throughout.

## Important Context
- All changes remain uncommitted; no commit or push made.
- Total scene files are new and not yet wired into `index.html`; `game.js` still uses the old static hotel SVG and 4 `LOCATIONS`.
- Planned 24 locations: Marlowe Hotel Room 814; Starlight Lounge rear office; Pier 9; Alcazar Arms Room 302; Blue Dahlia Diner Booth 3; Orpheum Theatre Dressing Room 2; Halcyon Warehouse Bay 7; Midnight Limited Sleeper Car 4; Radio KNOX Studio B; Golden Calf Pawnshop Shop 12; Sable Boathouse Slip 3; Vieux Carré Casino Room 6; Chapel of St. Jude Vestry; Ninth Street Garage Unit 5; Cactus Flower Greenhouse House 2; Fairview Mortuary Room 4; The Commodore Suite 1802; Rialto Alley Alley 7; Hall of Antiquities Gallery 3; Blue Note Barbershop Chair 2; Steam Laundry Basement; Ironworks Gym; Carnegie Library Wing 2; Palace Cinema Projection Booth.
- Planned in-scene sign text uses `location.plate` as `[topLabel, mainText]`, e.g. `['ROOM','814']`, `['PIER','9']`, `['BOOTH','3']`, `['CAR','4']`.
- Scene renderer signature: `renderScene(loc)` where `loc.scene` selects `SCENES[loc.scene]` and `loc.plate` feeds signage.
- Station metadata shape: `{ label, name, place }`; hotspot positions derive from `st.x / 400 * 100` and `st.y / 500 * 100`.
- `scene-core.js` palette keys are camelCase but emitted as kebab-case CSS vars (`floorLine` → `--floor-line`, etc.).
- `scene-stations.js` currently defines `null` placeholders for `coatChair`/`safeWall` then deletes them; these must be supplied.
- Existing office IDs and call flow remain: `#phoneZone`, `#phoneHint`, `#callCard`, `#callStatus`, `#callIdle`, `#callDialogue`, `#callLine`, `#callStep`, `#btnCallNext`, `#callAddress`, `#officeKicker`, `#officeSub`, `#btnSceneLabel`.
- `Sfx.startRing()` is gated by `state.call.answered`; toggling sound after answering must not restart ringing.
- On short screens, answered office state shifts lamp/phone upward to keep them above the taller dialogue card.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and polish a playable vertical-mobile noir detective game about solving randomized 1940s murder mysteries.
- Make every crime scene a visibly different place, with many varied locations, and place the room/pier number or name that Sergeant Miller says somewhere inside the scene.

## Requirements
- Dark, moody noir atmosphere with rain, shadows, and dramatic lighting; descriptions under two sentences.
- Each case randomizes victim, weapon, three suspects with motives/alibis, four clues including a smoking gun, and the true killer.
- Stages: 2:00 AM call, top-down crime scene with four inspectable objects, clue reveal, evidence board, accusation, win/loss.
- Incorrect accusation or accusing without the smoking gun loses; correct accusation after finding it wins.
- Vertical mobile layout with no scrolling.
- Office, lamp, phone, ringing, pickup, and sergeant dialogue must remain as previously improved.
- Crime scenes must not reuse the same room; user asked for “a bunch of different places… I mean alot.”
- The number/address Miller mentions must appear in-scene so each place feels distinct.

## Decisions
- Static HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with locally bundled fonts and custom SVG artwork.
- Audio remains optional and synthesized; no external runtime dependencies.
- Scene art is modular: shared renderer + palettes + ambient props + four focal stations + body outline + in-world signage.
- 24 locations/scenes now implemented, each with unique palette, floor/wall, props, body position, lighting, station skins, and sign style/placement.
- Station metadata shape `{ label, name, place }` drives hotspot tags, zoom/board labels, and clue phrasing.
- Scene art split into `scene-core.js`, `scene-props.js`, `scene-stations.js`, `scene-stations2.js`, and `scenes.js`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Randomized cases, clue logic, evidence board, accusation flow, victory/game-over logic.
- Noir office, crime scene, close-up, board, accusation, and end-screen views.
- Office visual upgrades, ringing animation, interactive call flow, synthesized audio, short-screen variants.
- `scene-core.js`: 24 palettes, shared SVG defs/patterns, room shell, body outline, 10 sign styles, `renderScene`, `getStationMeta`, `getStationPoint`, `drawSceneProp`; light opacity reduced to `.26`; palette vars convert camelCase to kebab-case.
- `scene-props.js`: ~40 ambient props including new `heavyBag`, `gymBench`, `washer`, `reelShelf`, `slotMachine`.
- `scene-stations.js`: 18 desk variants and 18 window/door variants.
- `scene-stations2.js`: 13 coat variants and 14 safe variants; defaults set as `STATIONS.desk/window/coat/safe`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build and polish a playable vertical-mobile noir detective game about solving randomized 1940s murder mysteries.
- Make every crime scene a visibly different place, with many varied locations, and place the room/pier number or name that Sergeant Miller says somewhere inside the scene.

## Requirements
- Dark, moody noir atmosphere with rain, shadows, and dramatic lighting; descriptions under two sentences.
- Each case randomizes victim, weapon, three suspects with motives/alibis, four clues including a smoking gun, and the true killer.
- Stages: 2:00 AM call, top-down crime scene with four inspectable objects, clue reveal, evidence board, accusation, win/loss.
- Incorrect accusation or accusing without the smoking gun loses; correct accusation after finding it wins.
- Vertical mobile layout with no scrolling.
- Office, lamp, phone, ringing, pickup, and sergeant dialogue must remain as previously improved.
- Crime scenes must not reuse the same room; user asked for “a bunch of different places… I mean alot.”
- The number/address Miller mentions must appear in-scene so each place feels distinct.

## Decisions
- Static HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with locally bundled fonts and custom SVG artwork.
- Audio remains optional and synthesized; no external runtime dependencies.
- Scene art is modular: shared renderer + palettes + ambient props + four focal stations + body outline + in-world signage.
- 24 locations/scenes implemented, each with unique palette, floor pattern, props, body position, lighting, station skins, and sign style/placement.
- Station metadata shape `{ label, name, place }` drives hotspot tags, zoom/board labels, and clue phrasing.
- Scene art split into `scene-core.js`, `scene-props.js`, `scene-stations.js`, `scene-stations2.js`, and `scenes.js`.
- Shared floor renders as a full-frame texture with wall texture only on the border frame; top-down room illusion comes from props/stations, not a distinct wall rect.

## Work State
### Completed
- Randomized cases, clue logic, evidence board, accusation flow, victory/game-over logic.
- Noir office, crime scene, close-up, board, accusation, and end-screen views.
- Office visual upgrades, ringing animation, interactive call flow, synthesized audio, short-screen variants.
- `scene-core.js`: 24 palettes, shared SVG defs/patterns, room shell, body outline, 10 sign styles, `renderScene`, `getStationMeta`, `getStationPoint`, `drawSceneProp`; light opacity `.26`; palette vars convert camelCase to kebab-case.
- `scene-props.js`: ~40 ambient props; added `heavyBag`, `gymBench`, `washer`, `reelShelf`, `slotMachine`, `barberChair`, `barberPole`, `mirror`, `laundryBasket`, `beam`, `filmCans`.
- `scene-stations.js`: 18 desk variants and 18 window/door variants; back door now has EXIT plate, push bar and threshold.
- `scene-stations2.js`: 13 coat variants and 14 safe variants; defaults set as `STATIONS.desk/window/coat/safe`.
- `scenes.js`: 24 scene specs (`marlowe`, `starlight`, `pier9`, `alcazar`, `diner`, `orpheum`, `warehouse`, `train`, `radio`, `pawnshop`, `boathouse`, `casino`, `chapel`, `garage`, `greenhouse`, `mortuary`, `commodore`, `rialto`, `gallery`, `barbershop`, `laundry`, `gym`, `library`, `cinema`).
- `index.html`: static hotel SVG replaced by `#sceneCanvas`; scene modules loaded before `game.js`; hotspots retained inside `#sceneArt`.
- `game.js`: 24 `LOCATIONS` with `scene`/`plate`/`feel`; previous-location avoidance; scene rendering on case start; hotspots positioned from station coords; dynamic station labels in scene/zoom/board; clue text uses station `place` phrases.
- Visual review of all 24 scenes completed; refreshed captures in `/tmp/opencode/shots/all/`.
- Composition fixes applied and verified: softened rug fill/border/shadow; darkened puddles; redrew chapel pews with legs/center aisle/hymnal; detailed car; gurney sheet/pillow/straps; couch cushions/legs/pillow; framed `shelves`; heavy bag chain reaches new gym ceiling beam; barbershop rebuilt with barber chair, mirror, pole; laundry counter has `kind:'laundry'` folded linens + basket; cinema changed to wood floor, removed folding screen, added film cans/cart, dimmer lights; Marlowe bed raised to `y:170`; Starlight stools moved to bar; garage car moved left/scaled, sign raised; chapel rug reduced to `176×136`; Rialto strongbox grounded on a crate.
- Verified 24 scenes at 390×844: no JS errors, no hotspot-tag overlaps, no tags outside scene, no page scroll (`scrollW=390`, `scrollH=844`).

### Active
- Final polish review of the refreshed 24 scenes.
- Planned but not yet applied: change chapel palette `rug`/`rugLine` from lavender to deep wine (or make a narrower aisle runner); remove floating `stand` prop from casino scene.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Change `chapel` palette rug colors to deep wine and/or narrow the chapel rug so it reads as a church runner.
2. Remove the floating `stand` prop from the casino scene (`x:330,y:176`).
3. Re-render affected scenes and spot-check chapel/casino/cinema.
4. Run full win/loss flow at `390×844`, `360×640`, and `320×568`: no scroll, call reset, hotspot labels, smoking-gun accusation, board/zoom labels, end screens.
5. Optionally increase sign top-label font sizes if location names are too small.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/Midnight-Detective/Midnight-Detective/game.js`: case generation, 24 locations, clue text, scene integration, call/accusation flow.
- `/home/runner/work/Midnight-Detective/Midnight-Detective/scenes.js`: 24 scene layouts, stations, props, lights, signs.
- `/home/runner/work/Midnight-Detective/Midnight-Detective/scene-core.js`: renderer, palettes, signage, room shell, station helpers.
- `/home/runner/work/Midnight-Detective/Midnight-Detective/scene-props.js`: ambient props and shared furniture art.
- `/home/runner/work/Midnight-Detective/Midnight-Detective/scene-stations.js`: desk/window/stage/back-door variants.
- `/home/runner/work/Midnight-Detective/Midnight-Detective/scene-stations2.js`: coat/safe variants and defaults.
- `/home/runner/work/Midnight-Detective/Midnight-Detective/index.html`: `#sceneCanvas`, hotspot markup, script order.
- `/home/runner/work/Midnight-Detective/Midnight-Detective/styles.css`: scene canvas, hotspot positioning, responsive sizing.
- `/tmp/opencode/all-scenes.mjs`: forces each location and captures refreshed scene screenshots.
- `/tmp/opencode/crop.mjs`: high-DPI scene crop helper.
- `/tmp/opencode/shots/all/`: 24 current scene screenshots after latest fixes.

## Important Context
- All changes are uncommitted; no commit or push made.
- Local test server runs at `http://127.0.0.1:4173/index.html` (`python3 -m http.server 4173 --bind 127.0.0.1`, PID in `/tmp/opencode/midnight-http.pid`).
- Playwright is available via `/home/runner/.local/share/omgithub-playwright` using `createRequire`.
- Element screenshots during the `roomIn` animation capture the wrong region; wait ~1s then use `page.screenshot({ clip: await locator.boundingBox() })`.
- `previousLocation` is a top-level `let`; `makeCase()` filters out the previous location name. Test forcing can temporarily replace `LOCATIONS` and set `previousLocation = null`.
- Station coords convert to hotspot percentages via `st.x / 400 * 100`, `st.y / 500 * 100`; tags use `data-side="top"` when station y > 56%.
- Scene SVG uses `preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"` and viewBox `0 0 400 500`; container aspect is 4/5.
- `window.__midnight` exposes `state`, `makeCase`, `startCase`, `openObject`, `goScene`, `goBoard`, `showScreen`, `showEnd`, `answerPhone`, `advanceCall`, `accuseIndex`, `Sfx`.
- `barberPole` uses an inline `clipPath id="rs-barber-clip"`; only one pole is drawn.
- New `beam` prop at `x:200,y:38,w:360` supports the gym heavy bag chain; high window draws over it.
- Existing office/call IDs remain: `#phoneZone`, `#phoneHint`, `#callCard`, `#callStatus`, `#callIdle`, `#callDialogue`, `#callLine`, `#callStep`, `#btnCallNext`, `#callAddress`, `#officeKicker`, `#officeSub`, `#btnSceneLabel`.

## The game

A short, replayable 1940s noir murder mystery built for vertical phone screens. Every case
randomizes the victim, the weapon, the three suspects, their motives and alibis, the four
clues, the true killer, and one of **24 hand-drawn crime scenes**. Each location carries the
room, pier, or suite number Miller gives you on the phone.

### How to play

1. **Answer the call.** Sergeant Miller gives you the address at 2:00 A.M.
2. **Work the scene.** Tap the four marked details to log clues. One of them is the smoking gun.
3. **Read the board.** Cross-check the evidence, motives, and alibis.
4. **Accuse once.** The right name with the smoking gun closes the case. The right name
   without it, or the wrong name, and the killer walks.

Rain, ringing, and clue sounds are optional — tap **SOUND** in the top corner to enable them.

### Run locally

There is no build step and no runtime dependency. Serve the folder with any static server:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 4173
```

Then open <http://127.0.0.1:4173/index.html>. Fonts and artwork are bundled; the game also
works when opened directly from disk.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finish and polish a playable vertical-mobile noir detective game about solving randomized 1940s murder mysteries.

## Requirements
- Dark, rainy 1940s noir atmosphere; scene descriptions stay under two sentences.
- Every case randomizes victim, weapon, three suspects with motives/alibis, four clues including a smoking gun, and the true killer.
- Flow: 2:00 AM call → top-down crime scene with four inspectable objects → clue reveal → evidence board → accusation → win/loss.
- Wrong accusation, or the correct name without the smoking gun, must lose; correct name with the gun must win.
- Vertical mobile layout with no scrolling; office, lamp, phone, ringing, pickup, and Miller dialogue must remain intact.
- Crime scenes must be visibly different places — “a bunch of different places… I mean alot.”
- The room/pier/suite number or name Miller gives must appear inside the scene.
- User’s latest instruction: “Continue where you left off and finish the game.”

## Decisions
- Static HTML/CSS/JavaScript with bundled fonts and custom SVG art; no runtime dependencies or build step.
- 24 unique locations, each with distinct palette, floor, props, body position, lighting, station skins, and sign style/placement.
- Scene art modularized across `scene-core.js`, `scene-props.js`, `scene-stations.js`, `scene-stations2.js`, `scenes.js`.
- Station metadata `{ label, name, place }` drives hotspot tags, zoom/board labels, and clue phrasing.
- Audio remains optional and synthesized via Web Audio.
- Responsive compromises: board clues allow three lines on short screens; scene description remains visible at all heights using compact styling.

## Work State
### Completed
- Full randomized case engine, clue logic, evidence board, accusation, win/loss/no-gun outcomes.
- 24 finished crime scenes with unique art and an in-scene sign matching Miller’s address.
- Office/call experience, optional sound, close-up, board, accusation, and end screens.
- Chapel rug recolored deep wine; floating casino stand and chair removed; radio sign now reads “STUDIO B” on one line.
- In-world sign top labels enlarged; all 24 addresses verified present.
- Generic chair prop redrawn as a recognizable top-down chair with backrest, seat, splayed legs, and armrests.
- Scene descriptions now visible on short phones (`@media (max-height:700px)` compact styling) without overlap or scrolling.
- Sound toggle given a larger invisible tap target; iOS web-app meta tags added.
- README expanded with game overview, how to play, and local-run instructions.
- 600-case generator audit: 0 problems; all 24 locations, 12 suspects, and 10 weapons observed.
- 24-scene render audit: 0 problems, 0 page errors, 4 hotspots each, no tag overlaps/overflow.
- Flow QA: **175/175 checks passed** across 390×844, 412×915, 375×667, 360×640, and 320×568.
- Verified 300/300 end screens show the actual smoking-gun clue under “THE NAIL.”
- `file://` launch works with no errors; desktop frames the game in a centered 480px device; landscape is usable.
- Firefox/WebKit are not installed in this environment; Chromium is fully tested.

### Active
- Final regression rerun of the flow suite after the scene-description CSS change.

### Blocked
- (none)

173: function sceneWalls(scene) {

175:   const pat = SCENE_WALLS[scene.wall] || 'rs-w-panel';

182:     <rect x="0" y="477" width="${dx}" height="23" fill="${wallFill}"/>
183:     <rect x="${dx + dw}" y="477" width="${400 - dx - dw}" height="23" fill="${wallFill}"/>
184:     <rect x="0" y="0" width="400" height="23" fill="url(#${pat})"/>
185:     <rect x="0" y="0" width="21" height="500" fill="url(#${pat})"/>
186:     <rect x="379" y="0" width="21" height="500" fill="url(#${pat})"/>
187:     <rect x="0" y="477" width="${dx}" height="23" fill="url(#${pat})"/>
188:     <rect x="${dx + dw}" y="477" width="${400 - dx - dw}" height="23" fill="url(#${pat})"/>
189:     <g fill="var(--wall-hi)" opacity=".5">
190:       <rect x="21" y="20" width="358" height="3"/>
191:       <rect x="18" y="23" width="3" height="454"/>
192:       <rect x="379" y="23" width="3" height="454"/>
193:       <rect x="21" y="474" width="${dx - 21}" height="3"/>
194:       <rect x="${dx + dw}" y="474" width="${379 - dx - dw}" height="3"/>
195:     </g>
196:     <g fill="#000" opacity=".35">
197:       <rect x="0" y="23" width="400" height="4"/>
198:       <rect x="21" y="0" width="4" height="500"/>
199:       <rect x="375" y="0" width="4" height="500"/>
200:     </g>`;
201:   const doorArt = () => {
202:     if (door.style === 'none') {
203:       return `<rect x="${dx}" y="477" width="${dw}" height="23" fill="var(--wall)"/><rect x="${dx}" y="477" width="${dw}" height="23" fill="url(#${pat})"/>`;
204:     }
205:     const metal = door.style === 'metal';
206:     const fill = metal ? 'var(--metal)' : 'var(--wood)';
207:     const leaf = `<polygon points="${dx + 5},477 ${dx + 19},438 ${dx + dw - 18},440 ${dx + dw - 5},477" fill="${fill}" stroke="#120c09" stroke-width="1.3"/>
208:       <polygon points="${dx + 13},470 ${dx + 22},445 ${dx + dw - 21},447 ${dx + dw - 13},470" fill="#000" opacity=".22"/>
209:       <path d="M${dx + 18} 474 L${dx + 27} 450" stroke="var(--wall-hi)" stroke-width="1" opacity=".35"/>
210:       <circle cx="${dx + dw - 22}" cy="460" r="2.4" fill="var(--metal-hi)" opacity=".8"/>`;
211:     return `<rect x="${dx}" y="477" width="${dw}" height="23" fill="#070809"/>
212:       <ellipse cx="${dx + dw / 2}" cy="481" rx="${dw * .45}" ry="9" fill="#d9b477" opacity=".07"/>
213:       ${leaf}`;
214:   };
215:   return bands + doorArt();
216: }

## Objective
- Finish and polish a playable vertical-mobile noir detective game with randomized 1940s murder mysteries, now specifically improving the zoom-in feature so it animates convincingly and every close-up matches the object shown in the crime scene.

## Requirements
- Dark, rainy 1940s noir atmosphere; scene descriptions under two sentences.
- Every case randomizes victim, weapon, three suspects with motives/alibis, four clues including a smoking gun, and the true killer.
- Flow: 2:00 AM call → top-down crime scene with four inspectable objects → clue reveal → evidence board → accusation → win/loss.
- Wrong accusation, or correct name without the smoking gun, must lose; correct name with the gun must win.
- Vertical mobile layout with no scrolling; office, lamp, phone, ringing, pickup, and Miller dialogue must remain intact.
- 24 visibly distinct crime scenes; Miller’s room/pier/suite name must appear inside each scene.
- User’s latest instruction: “Improve the Zoom in feature, make it an actual animation that zooms in, and then also the zoomed in object should look like how it looked before it was zoomed in… each zoomed in object should fit its zoomed out object, like the windows… the clothes, the tables and all the objects, so work on it to make it look good.”

## Decisions
- Static HTML/CSS/JavaScript with bundled fonts and SVG art; no runtime dependencies or build step.
- Replaced four generic reusable close-up illustrations with a procedural close-up camera that crops the actual rendered crime-scene SVG around the selected station, so the zoomed object is pixel-identical to the scene object.
- Added a camera push-in transition using a cloned scene SVG in a fixed overlay; it scales/translates from the scene-art frame to the exact close-up crop and crossfades into the zoom screen.
- Close-ups add atmospheric vignette, focus glow, dust, subtle weave on garments, and dynamic magnification labels.
- Close-up station bounding boxes are read from live SVG `getBBox()` rather than hand-authored per-scene art.
- Audio remains optional and synthesized via Web Audio.
- Responsive compromises retained: board clues allow three lines on short screens; scene description stays visible at all heights.

## Work State
### Completed
- Full randomized case engine, clue logic, evidence board, accusation, win/loss/no-gun outcomes.
- 24 finished crime scenes with unique art and address signage matching Miller’s address.
- Office/call experience, optional sound, close-up, board, accusation, and end screens.
- Prior visual fixes: chapel rug, casino stand/chair, radio “STUDIO B,” enlarged sign labels, redrawn generic chair, short-phone scene description, enlarged sound tap target, iOS meta tags, README.
- Prior QA: 600-case generator audit 0 problems; 24-scene audit 0 problems; flow QA 175/175; 300/300 correct smoking-gun text; `file://` launch works.
- Zoom rework implemented:
  - Added `scene-closeups.js` with `renderCloseup()`, `getCloseupFrame()`, `closeupDust()`, `CLOSEUP_DEFS`.
  - Station groups in `scene-core.js` are now wrapped with `data-station` attributes.
  - `renderZoom()` now uses `renderCloseup()` and sets dynamic `MAGNIFIED · NX`.
  - Added zoom transition overlay markup/CSS and `beginZoomIn()`/`cancelZoomTransit()` in `game.js`.
  - Removed the old unused `CLOSEUPS` illustration block from `game.js`.
  - Flow suite still passes 175/175 after the rework.
  - Close-up screenshots verified for porthole, high window, card table, diner table, stole, coat, cage, and cabinet; shapes/identity now match their scene objects.
  - Animation frames captured for pier porthole; overlay starts from the room and expands to the close-up bay.
- Updated `README.md` with game overview, how to play, and local-run instructions.

### Active
- Visual polish and audit of the full 24-scene × 4-object close-up set.
- Verify the final animation-to-close-up alignment at the end of the push-in, not just the static close-up.
- Decide whether the full-scene crop is the final visual approach or requires further atmosphere/detail refinement.

### Blocked
- Firefox and WebKit are unavailable in this environment; Chromium is fully testable.

## Next Move
1. View `/tmp/opencode/shots/anim-*.png` to confirm the push-in sequence and final alignment.
2. Build/run a 24-scene × 4-object close-up audit: no page errors, correct station markup in `#zoomCanvas`, bbox fully inside the close-up viewBox, and screenshots for all 96 close-ups.
3. Make a contact sheet or visually inspect all 24 scenes’ four close-ups, especially unusual stations (doors, portholes, cabinets, garment racks, safes).
4. Re-run `node /tmp/opencode/flow.mjs`, `node /tmp/opencode/scenes.mjs`, and `node /tmp/opencode/invariants.mjs`.
5. Check `file://` launch, add/reduce zoom-out polish if needed, and update README/QA if behavior changes.
6. Do not commit or push unless the user asks.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/Midnight-Detective/Midnight-Detective/scene-closeups.js`: new procedural close-up renderer and camera crop logic.
- `/home/runner/work/Midnight-Detective/Midnight-Detective/game.js`: renderZoom, openObject, zoom transition functions, screen flow.
- `/home/runner/work/Midnight-Detective/Midnight-Detective/scene-core.js`: scene renderer; station groups now expose `data-station`.
- `/home/runner/work/Midnight-Detective/Midnight-Detective/index.html`: zoom markup/caption, transition overlay, script loading.
- `/home/runner/work/Midnight-Detective/Midnight-Detective/styles.css`: zoom screen, transition overlay, responsive/no-scroll styling.
- `/home/runner/work/Midnight-Detective/Midnight-Detective/scenes.js`: 24 scene layouts and station selections.
- `/home/runner/work/Midnight-Detective/Midnight-Detective/scene-stations.js`: desk/window station art.

## Important Context

- Transition overlay is `.zoom-transit` / `#zoomTransit`, frame `#zoomTransitFrame`, veil `.zoom-transit-veil`; overlay is z-index 70, below global grain/vignette.
- Reduced-motion users skip the animated push-in; `prefersReducedMotion()` is checked in `beginZoomIn()`.
- Current close-up visual approach crops the complete scene around the station, preserving the exact station art and surrounding context; earlier isolated-hero/blur version was tested and rejected as less natural.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finish and polish a playable vertical-mobile noir detective game with randomized 1940s murder mysteries, now specifically ensuring the zoom-in is a real camera animation and every close-up is the exact object shown in the crime scene.

## Requirements
- Dark, rainy 1940s noir atmosphere; scene descriptions under two sentences.
- Every case randomizes victim, weapon, three suspects with motives/alibis, four clues including a smoking gun, and the true killer.
- Flow: 2:00 AM call → top-down crime scene with four inspectable objects → clue reveal → evidence board → accusation → win/loss.
- Wrong accusation, or correct name without the smoking gun, must lose; correct name with the gun must win.
- Vertical mobile layout with no scrolling; office, lamp, phone, ringing, pickup, and Miller dialogue must remain intact.
- 24 visibly distinct crime scenes; Miller’s room/pier/suite name must appear inside each scene.
- User’s latest instruction: “Improve the Zoom in feature, make it an actual animation that zooms in, and then also the zoomed in object should look like how it looked before it was zoomed in… each zoomed in object should fit its zoomed out object, like the windows… the clothes, the tables and all the objects, so work on it to make it look good.”

## Decisions
- Static HTML/CSS/JavaScript with bundled fonts/SVG art; no build step or runtime dependencies.
- Replaced four generic reusable close-up illustrations with a procedural close-up camera that crops the actual rendered scene SVG around the selected station.
- Push-in transition uses a cloned scene SVG in a fixed overlay, scaling/translating from the scene canvas to the exact close-up station rect, then crossfading into the zoom screen.
- Transition now measures the selected station’s live bounding rect on both the room clone and the close-up copy and matches size/center exactly, absorbing SVG slice rounding.

## The game

A short, replayable 1940s noir murder mystery built for vertical phone screens. Every case
randomizes the victim, the weapon, the three suspects, their motives and alibis, the four
clues, the true killer, and one of **24 hand-drawn crime scenes**. Each location carries the
room, pier, or suite number Miller gives you on the phone.

### How to play

1. **Answer the call.** Sergeant Miller gives you the address at 2:00 A.M.
2. **Work the scene.** Tap the four marked details to log clues. One of them is the smoking gun.
3. **Read the board.** Cross-check the evidence, motives, and alibis.
4. **Accuse once.** The right name with the smoking gun closes the case. The right name
   without it, or the wrong name, and the killer walks.

Every tap pushes the camera into the room and inspects the object that is actually there; leaving
pulls the camera back out the same way. The close-up is cropped from the same scene drawing, so a
porthole stays a porthole and a coat stays the same coat.

Rain, ringing, and clue sounds are optional — tap **SOUND** in the top corner to enable them.

### Run locally

There is no build step and no runtime dependency. Serve the folder with any static server:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 4173
```

Then open <http://127.0.0.1:4173/index.html>. Fonts and artwork are bundled; the game also
works when opened directly from disk.

A short, replayable 1940s noir murder mystery built for vertical phone screens. Every case
randomizes the victim, the weapon, the three suspects, their motives and alibis, the clues,
the true killer, and one of **24 hand-drawn crime scenes**. Each location carries the
room, pier, or suite number Miller gives you on the phone.

Each scene deals a different number of inspectable details — anywhere from **3 to 8** — and
never repeats the same count the next time you visit that location. The loose evidence
(ashtrays, matchbooks, watches, gloves, and so on) is unique within a scene, so no two
objects on the same board are ever the same.

### How to play

1. **Answer the call.** Sergeant Miller gives you the address at 2:00 A.M.
2. **Work the scene.** Tap each marked detail to log a clue. Exactly one is the smoking gun.
3. **Read the board.** Cross-check the evidence, motives, and alibis.
4. **Accuse once.** The right name with the smoking gun closes the case. The right name
   without it, or the wrong name, and the killer walks.

## Objective
- Finish the playable vertical-mobile noir detective game and its randomized mystery system.
- Add 3–8 unique inspectable objects per case, varying the count when a location recurs.

## Requirements
- Preserve the rainy 1940s noir atmosphere and call → scene → clues → evidence board → accusation → outcome flow.
- Keep the office, lamp, phone, ringing, pickup, and Miller dialogue intact; support vertical mobile layouts without scrolling.
- Keep all 24 scenes distinct, with correct Miller location names and close-ups matching their source objects.
- Use static HTML/CSS/JavaScript with bundled assets, no build step or runtime dependencies; audio remains optional and synthesized with Web Audio.
- Each scene should have 3–8 different inspectable objects; a recurring location should not repeat its previous object count.

## Decisions
- Generate close-ups by cropping the rendered crime-scene SVG rather than using generic illustrations.
- Animate a scene snapshot to the selected station’s measured rect, crossfade into the close-up, and mirror the camera move on exit; provide a reduced-motion fallback.
- Keep the four authored room stations visible as scene set dressing; draw additional evidence stations only when selected for the case.
- Track object-count history per location, avoiding previously used counts until its count cycle is exhausted.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented and QA’d the existing case flow, 24 crime scenes, procedural close-ups, and bidirectional camera transitions.
- Earlier QA passed: 216/216 camera moves aligned within 0.6 px; zero layout overflow at 8 viewport sizes; zero console errors or failed requests; 24/24 scenes had matching location names and briefs.
- Added `scene-items.js` with 19 loose-evidence station drawings and station-family metadata.
- Updated markup for generated hotspots and detail labels; loaded `scene-items.js`.
- Updated `scene-core.js` so `renderScene(loc, objects)` can selectively render authored and chosen stations.
- Began replacing fixed four-object case generation with randomized objects and clue assembly in `game.js`.

### Active
- Complete integration of the variable-object system across rendering, hotspot interaction, close-ups, evidence board, accusation logic, and case completion.
- Test object-count variation, unique objects, clue solvability, camera transitions, and mobile layouts.

### Blocked
- `game.js` still has legacy fixed-object references (`OBJECT_ORDER`, `OBJECTS`, four-clue progress, etc.) in functions such as `renderCase`, `renderSceneState`, `renderZoom`, and `renderBoard`; the new variable-object data is not yet fully integrated and may currently break gameplay.

## Next Move
1. Finish converting remaining `game.js` consumers from fixed objects to `caseData.objects` and per-case clue keys; ensure core stations are available in each candidate pool.
2. Update hotspot generation and positioning to use each object’s station coordinates and its slot metadata; verify `renderScene(c.location, c.objects)` filters correctly.
3. Audit close-up rendering, clue navigation, evidence board, gun/no-gun outcomes, accusation readiness, and reset behavior for variable object counts.
4. Run automated and tap-driven tests across counts 3–8, repeated locations, all endings, reduced motion, and mobile viewports; fix any layout or logic regressions.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: case generation, clue flow, board, accusation, and camera transitions; variable-object integration is incomplete.
- `scene-items.js`: loose evidence art, extra-item pool, and station-family metadata.
- `scene-core.js`: crime-scene renderer and station markers; `renderScene` now accepts selected objects.
- `scene-stations.js`: authored desk/window station definitions.
- `scene-stations2.js`: authored coat/safe station definitions.
- `scenes.js`: 24 scene layouts and station placements.
- `scene-closeups.js`: procedural close-up crop and focus treatment.
- `index.html`: scene markup and script loading.
- `styles.css`: responsive layout and zoom transitions.
- `README.md`: gameplay, local run, and zoom documentation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted and unpushed.
- The latest edits replaced fixed case generation with count history, seeded location extras, randomized object selection, and clue assembly; verify syntax and runtime before further changes.
- A local audit script was created at `/tmp/opencode/audit/boardmeasure.mjs`; a local HTTP server was started on port `4173`.
- Prior final captures and audit sheets are at `/tmp/opencode/shots/final-scene.png`, `/tmp/opencode/shots/final-zoom.png`, and `/tmp/opencode/shots/closeup-sheet-{1..4}.png`.

1. When you zoom in (close-up view of an object), you can interact with the objects — e.g., click/tap parts of the close-up to discover things. They believe we already added that but it doesn't work anymore.

Random so the game feels complete with lots of random variations each playthrough.

So we need to design an interaction system in the close-up: secondary hotspots inside the zoomed artifact (e.g., drawer, underside, inside pocket) that reveal the clue. Right now, the clue is displayed immediately in the zoom view's clue sheet. Actually the current flow: openObject(key) immediately logs the clue and shows the text in the clue sheet. Plan:
- Zoom close-up shows the object art. Add interactive "probe" regions inside the close-up (rendered as subtle glints/reticles) tied to each object's possible interaction slots.
- Each object type (desk/window/coat/safe + loose evidence types) gets a set of interaction spots with labels and reveal animations.
- The clue is only logged when the player finds the right interaction (or perhaps searches). But the user says "each objects should have a few different interactions on each scene", e.g., a note on the table one time, in a drawer another time, a different clue in the drawer another time. So randomness: the clue's hiding place varies per case and per location, and the content varies (clue type).

Design decision: Keep it simple but rich. In zoom view:
- Show 3–4 interactive "search spots" on the object (e.g., desk: tabletop, drawer, underside, letter tray; safe: dial, door, shelf, floor beneath; coat: pocket, lining, collar, sleeve; window: latch, sill, pane, curtain; plus per-loose-object spots).
- Each spot is tappable, with a subtle marker. Tapping a spot reveals a micro-description ("Drawer: empty. Just dust and a bent paperclip.") and, if that spot holds the actual clue for this case, reveals the clue text and logs it.
- The clue object's hidden spot is randomized per case; also the non-clue spots produce randomized flavor text, some of which can reference alternate clue types ("a matchbook", "a betting slip")—the user's example is that different visits put different clue types in different places.
- Also, perhaps for the *clue itself*, the hiding place data should be generated per case: `clue.spot` index and `spot label`. Each object has several possible spots; choose one at case build.

But requirement also says "each object should have a few different interactions on each scene, ... it should be random so the game feels complete, lots of random things that can happen each time should be different." So the interaction discoveries themselves should vary: each time you play, the object's drawers/pockets contain random items, and the clue may be in a different one. We could generate for each object a set of 3–5 slots each with content: one clue slot, and fillers randomly drawn from a pool of flavor finds (some mundane, some red herrings). The filler content could even be small bonuses that add notes to the board? Keep focused: make interactions produce flavor text + optional secondary note that appears in the zoom panel. The clue is only awarded when found.

However, the existing loop logs the clue on open. Changing to require finding the hidden spot adds gameplay. Need to ensure accusation readiness: player must find the gun clue. The clue sheet currently shows clue text immediately. We can show "SEARCH THE DESK" until found, then reveal the clue sheet with text and log it. Once found, revisiting shows it already revealed.

We must ensure the flow: openObject(key) → zoom view; the close-up shows object with 2–4 interaction hotspots. The HUD "FOUND x / N" updates only when clue found. ### Feature: Close-up investigation

When a player taps a detail hotspot in the room, they zoom into the object. Currently the clue is auto-logged and fully shown. New behavior:

1. The close-up becomes searchable. The object art is the hero, surrounded by a dimmed room. Place 2–4 "search points" on the object (interactive buttons styled as small pulsing glints/reticles), each at a location specific to the object type.
2. Each search point has a label (e.g., DRAWER, TABLETOP, UNDERSIDE, TRAY for desk). Tapping reveals an interaction "find": text in the clue sheet and a stamp like LOGGED, or "NOTHING HERE" note. Randomized per case:

   - The other spots hold random flavor discoveries. Some flavor discoveries may themselves be mini-clues? The user wants "each objects should have a few different interactions on each scene" and "one time there can be a note on the table, other time it could be in a drawer, other time there could be a different clue in the drawer that's no note" — that mostly means the hidden clue's location and content varies. We can achieve:
     - For each case and object: randomly choose which search spot holds the real clue.
     - For non-clue spots: randomly draw a flavor item from a per-kind pool (e.g., desk: matchbook, phone number, bent paperclip, cigarette burn...). These flavor texts should vary across cases too. Some can be "empty" lines.
     - The clue assignment (which object holds gun/red/etc.) already varies per case via buildClues.
3. The clue sheet shows the interaction result, not automatically the clue. Before any interaction: prompt text "SEARCH THE DESK — TAP A LIT SPOT" with clue count indicator. On tapping a spot:
   - If it's the clue spot: reveal clue text with type styling, mark logged, update found set, announce.
   - If flavor: show flavor text, mark spot as searched (fades), keep clue unfound. Player can tap another. No penalty.
   - Once clue found, other spots can still be tapped for flavor (nice optional content).
4. State: `state.found` currently tracks objects whose clues are logged. We add `state.searched` map: key -> Set(spotIndex) per case. When leaving and returning, reveal states persist. On new case, reset.

The SVG fills the bay with slice, so the scale is max(bayW/frame.w, bayH/frame.h) and content is centered. Given a point in room coordinates (px,py), compute rendered position:
  - scale = max(bayW/frame.w, bayH/frame.h)
  - contentW = frame.w*scale; contentH = frame.h*scale
  - offsetX = (bayW - contentW)/2; offsetY = (bayH - contentH)/2

  - y = offsetY + (py - frame.y)*scale

## Objective
- Complete the playable vertical-mobile noir detective game and its randomized mystery system.
- Give each case 3–8 unique inspectable objects, varying the count when a location recurs.

## Requirements
- Preserve the rainy 1940s noir atmosphere and call → scene → clues → evidence board → accusation → outcome flow.
- Keep the office, lamp, phone, ringing, pickup, and Miller dialogue intact; support vertical mobile layouts without scrolling.
- Keep all 24 scenes distinct, with correct Miller location names and close-ups matching their source objects.
- Use static HTML/CSS/JavaScript with bundled assets and no build step or runtime dependencies; audio remains optional and synthesized with Web Audio.

## Decisions
- Generate close-ups by cropping the rendered crime-scene SVG, not with generic illustrations.
- Animate scene snapshots to measured station positions and mirror the camera move on exit, with reduced-motion support.
- Keep four authored room stations visible as set dressing; draw additional evidence stations only when selected for the case.
- Track object-count history per location; avoid repeating a count until its cycle is exhausted.

- Integrated selected evidence stations, generated hotspots and labels, procedural close-ups, and bidirectional camera transitions.

A short, replayable 1940s noir murder mystery built for vertical phone screens. Every case
randomizes the victim, the weapon, the three suspects, their motives and alibis, the clues,
the true killer, and one of **24 hand-drawn crime scenes**. Each location carries the
room, pier, or suite number Miller gives you on the phone.

Each scene deals a different number of inspectable details — anywhere from **3 to 8** — and
never repeats the same count the next time you visit that location. The loose evidence
(ashtrays, matchbooks, watches, gloves, and so on) is unique within a scene, so no two
objects on the same board are ever the same.

### How to play

1. **Answer the call.** Sergeant Miller gives you the address at 2:00 A.M.
2. **Work the scene.** Tap each marked detail to log a clue. Exactly one is the smoking gun.
3. **Read the board.** Cross-check the evidence, motives, and alibis.
4. **Accuse once.** The right name with the smoking gun closes the case. The right name
   without it, or the wrong name, and the killer walks.

Every tap pushes the camera into the room and inspects the object that is actually there; leaving
pulls the camera back out the same way. The close-up is cropped from the same scene drawing, so a
porthole stays a porthole and a coat stays the same coat.

Rain, ringing, and clue sounds are optional — tap **SOUND** in the top corner to enable them.

### Run locally

There is no build step and no runtime dependency. Serve the folder with any static server:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 4173
```

Then open <http://127.0.0.1:4173/index.html>. Fonts and artwork are bundled; the game also
works when opened directly from disk.

messages.text: "Now make it so when you zoom in, you can interact with the objects, I believe we already added that but it looks like it doesn't work anymore, but then I also want it to be different for each object, and also each objects should have a few different interactions on each scene, so for example one time there can be a note on the table, other time it could be in a drawer, other time there could be a different clue in the draw that's no note, you get it, it should be random so rhe game feels complete, lots of random things that can happen each time should be different, you should be able to tap on the objects to do stuff to it, it shouldn't just be logged onto the evidence board, it needs to feel like the player discovered the clue"

So they want tangible interactions on the object in zoom, like tapping object parts that "do stuff" (open drawer, move object, etc.), not just click a spot and the clue auto-logs. We need enhance interactions: animate object manipulation, perhaps a two-step discovery where tapping a spot reveals something (glint/slip) then player taps the revealed clue to collect. Also different interactions per object: e.g., drag/open drawer, lift hat, turn over, open lid. We need make it feel discovered: tap a spot to search → a reaction animation and text → if clue, reveal a physical clue token on the object; player taps "COLLECT" or the revealed clue to log. Maybe a "hold to open" mechanic? The user's main request is to make zoom objects interactive and discovery-based, not just auto-log. We also have a failing board layout at 320x480 n=6 due to longer clue text. Need fix that too. Let's plan the new interaction model: Current: each object has 3-4 search spots, each a button. Tapping searches; if clue, logs immediately. User wants: - tap on objects to do stuff (open, lift, turn, pull). - shouldn't just be logged; player discovers the clue. We can add a two-stage interaction: 1. Tap a search spot (drawer, pocket, lid, etc.) → the spot triggers a physical "action" animation: e.g., drawer slides open, lid lifts, cloth lifts, object rotates, etc. The close-up art could animate via CSS on the relevant station group? We can manipulate the SVG clone to animate. Since the close-up is a cropped clone of scene SVG, we can find `[data-station=key]` and animate transform within the close-up. But action semantics vary by spot. Could animate a generic reaction: a subtle shake/lift of the object, a dust puff, and a "revealed" overlay token at the spot. More specific: add a revealed "clue item" icon at the searched point (folded note, bullet, key, etc.) with a glow, and a "TAKE" button. The player must tap the revealed item to log it. For false leads, reveal a small debris token (matchstick, button, ash) and a line; no log. That strongly conveys discovery. 2. When clue found by searching, don't immediately add to found. Instead reveal a "clue card" token in the art at the spot, with a pulsing "TAKE" label. The player taps it to collect; only then `state.found.add(key)` and the clue logs. This directly meets "It shouldn't just be logged onto the evidence board, it needs to feel like the player discovered the clue." Also "tap on the objects to do stuff to it": We can make each search spot have an **action** verb and a small animation: - Drawer/tray/till/tool drawer: slides open (translate the station art?). - Lid/cover/cap: lift/rotate. - Pocket/lining/collar/cuff/hem: rustle/flap. - Dial/lock/hinge: turn/rattle. - Windowsill/latch/pane/glass: light glint/wipe. - Underside/base: tilt/lift object. - Tabletop/bench/counter: brush dust. - Trinket parts: rotate/flip/wipe. Implementing true SVG part animations is hard because part geometry isn't separated. Maybe too weird. - `action-wipe`: a moving sheen across the point. - `action-rattle`: quick shake. Since the close-up has the station group, we can add classes to it. But the search spot layer is separate; we can add visual effects at the probe point: dust puff, sparkle, and a revealed token. Maybe better and more feasible: On tap, show a **probe pulse** at the spot (expanding ring) and perform a small camera punch-in to the spot, plus an **object reaction** via CSS transform of the close-up SVG or station group. Then reveal the token. This will feel tactile. Need careful with the existing artifact: The closeup SVG clone has all scene elements; station group has `data-station`. We can select it and animate a class. But transform origin relative to crop? We can set `transform-box: fill-box; transform-origin: center;` in CSS for `.closeup-svg [data-station]` and animate with keyframes. That should work. For clue discovery: - When the correct spot is searched, set `plan.revealed = index` (or state per object) and show a clue token at the spot, reading "CLUE" / maybe the object's clue type icon (gun, note, etc.). - The clue sheet shows a **partial discovery** message: "Your fingers catch paper. The spot-level probe effect + token is the real interaction. We can still add subtle motion: - `open`: station group shifts/rotates slightly and a dark gap overlay grows at the token? More useful: make the object station itself respond with a subtle idle animation on tap? Hmm. The phrase "you should be able to tap on the objects to do stuff to it" likely means tapping search spots should perform actions (open drawer, etc.), not just auto-log. Our two-stage reveal meets it. messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete the playable vertical-mobile noir detective game and its randomized mystery system.
- Give each case 3–8 unique inspectable objects, varying the count when a location recurs.

## Requirements
- Preserve the rainy 1940s noir atmosphere and call → scene → clues → evidence board → accusation → outcome flow.
- Keep the office, lamp, phone, ringing, pickup, and Miller dialogue intact; support vertical mobile layouts without scrolling.
- Keep all 24 scenes distinct, with correct Miller location names and close-ups matching their source objects.
- Use static HTML/CSS/JavaScript with bundled assets and no build step or runtime dependencies; audio remains optional and synthesized with Web Audio.

## Decisions
- Generate close-ups by cropping the rendered crime-scene SVG, not with generic illustrations.
- Animate scene snapshots to measured station positions and mirror the camera move on exit, with reduced-motion support.
- Keep four authored room stations visible as set dressing; draw additional evidence stations only when selected for the case.
- Track object-count history per location; avoid repeating a count until its cycle is exhausted.
- Each object has three or four randomized search spots, one of which holds its clue; only one room clue is the smoking gun.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented variable 3–8 object cases, clue assembly, dynamic board and accusation logic, and case reset.
- Integrated selected evidence stations, generated hotspots and labels, procedural close-ups, and bidirectional camera transitions.
- Improved clue-sheet behavior after a clue is found, varied search flavor and hiding-place wording, and updated README gameplay details.
- Adjusted search-spot styling and reduced-motion transition delays.

### Active
- Final verification of recent search-flow, responsive, reduced-motion, and board changes; the latest recorded action ran `/tmp/opencode/audit/board4.mjs`, but its results are unavailable.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Review the latest board audit result if available, then run any needed final checks and summarize the changes.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: case generation, search plans, clue flow, board, accusation, and camera transitions.
- `scene-items.js`: loose-evidence artwork and station metadata.
- `scene-core.js`: crime-scene rendering and station markers.
- `scene-closeups.js`: procedural close-up crop and focus treatment.
- `index.html`: scene markup and script loading.
- `styles.css`: responsive layout, search-spot styling, and zoom transitions.
- `README.md`: gameplay and implementation documentation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted and unpushed.
- Earlier reported QA passed for generated cases, close-ups, camera alignment, board/mobile layout, endings/reset, and reduced motion.
- Recent search-flow and responsiveness audits were run, but their results are unavailable in this record.

- 🧬 [Explore the remix source](https://github.com/DJBS1868/Midnight-Detective).
<!-- omgithub:readme:end -->

## The game

A short, replayable 1940s noir murder mystery built for vertical phone screens. Every case
randomizes the victim, the weapon, the three suspects, their motives and alibis, the clues,
the true killer, and one of **24 hand-drawn crime scenes**. Each location carries the
room, pier, or suite number Miller gives you on the phone.

Each scene deals a different number of inspectable details — anywhere from **3 to 8** — and
never repeats the same count the next time you visit that location. The loose evidence
(ashtrays, matchbooks, watches, gloves, and so on) is unique within a scene, so no two
objects on the same board are ever the same.

### How to play

1. **Answer the call.** Sergeant Miller gives you the address at 2:00 A.M.
2. **Work the scene.** Tap each marked detail to inspect it. Every object hides **three or
   four search spots** — a drawer, a pocket, a windowsill, a latch. One spot holds the clue;
   the others hold fresh debris and false leads. Exactly one clue in the room is the smoking gun.
3. **Read the board.** Cross-check the evidence, motives, and alibis.
4. **Accuse once.** The right name with the smoking gun closes the case. The right name
   without it, or the wrong name, and the killer walks.

Every tap pushes the camera into the room and inspects the object that is actually there; leaving
pulls the camera back out the same way. The close-up is cropped from the same scene drawing, so a
porthole stays a porthole and a coat stays the same coat. Search spots are placed on the object
itself, and both the hiding place and the debris are re-rolled for every new case, so the same
desk can hide a note in the drawer tonight and a gun under the blotter tomorrow.

Rain, ringing, and clue sounds are optional — tap **SOUND** in the top corner to enable them.

### Run locally

There is no build step and no runtime dependency. Serve the folder with any static server:

Implemented and verified the object-interaction and clue-discovery flow.

### What changed

- **Two-stage clue discovery** in `game.js`
  - Searching the correct spot now reveals a physical clue token inside the close-up instead of instantly logging it.
  - The status changes to `CLUE FOUND · TAP TO TAKE`, and only tapping the token adds the clue to the evidence board.
  - Revealed findings survive leaving and re-entering the scene; they still must be taken.
  - Already-logged clues can be reviewed normally.

- **Per-object interaction feedback**
  - Tapping a search spot now produces a ripple at the point and a physical beat on the object itself: open, lift, turn, pull, or wipe, chosen from the spot being searched.
  - Clue tokens show an icon matching the finding type — note, gun, weapon, alibi, or red herring — plus a `TAKE` label.
  - Added a subtle discovery sound and camera flash when the clue is collected.

- **Randomized search variety**
  - Each case still rerolls the hiding spot, remaining debris, clue type, and clue text placement.
  - Multiple objects on a scene expose different spot vocabularies and interactions, while the same object can hide its clue somewhere different next case.

- **Accessibility and layout**
  - Keyboard flow works: focus a spot, press Enter to reveal, focus moves to the finding, Enter takes it.
  - Reduced-motion mode skips camera transitions but keeps the interaction and token flow.
  - Clue tokens and search pips stay clamped inside the zoom bay across phone sizes.

- **Docs**
  - Updated `README.md` to explain that a finding must be taken before it reaches the board.

### Verification

Ran browser audits at 320×568 through 430×932:

- Real pointer/touch taps on search pips work.
- Searching never increments the board count; taking the token does.
- Reveal persists across scene exits.
- Keyboard reveal/take works.
- Reduced-motion mode completes in ~100 ms with no transit overlay.
- All 24 locations and 101+ stations produce 3–4 spots with valid clue placement.
- 150 generated cases stayed within 3–8 objects with no unresolved clue placeholders.
- Eight-detail boards fit at 320×568 with no horizontal or page overflow.
- Full case lifecycle reaches the correct win ending with the smoking gun.

Changes are in `game.js`, `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `README.md`; they remain uncommitted.
